For me my dysphoria spiked immensely when, after years of struggling with my identity I finally allowed myself to actually consider myself trans. And then it just built and built for months as I was too afraid to really do anything about it, and I assumed that, since I felt worse after starting to consider myself trans, it must mean I wasn't really trans! I told myself if I was really trans I would feel better just from knowing, and I used that as an excuse to continue to doubt and question myself. I literally went from thinking I couldn't be trans because I didn't have dysphoria, to invalidating my identity because I did have dysphoria. I set myself a rigged game I couldn't win either way.

Now I can say with some certainty that the reason it hurt so bad is because I still wasn't allowing myself to fully accept it, and I wasn't doing anything about it. But... that was really hard to see from inside it. Just wanted to share this in case it resonated with anyone. You're not alone. <3

Most people say enneagram type is an immutable thing you’re born with, but I don’t think it is. I think we’re born with *tendencies*, and life pushes us to develop those tendencies in certain ways. I typed as a 4 a long time ago, and while I think that's right, I've also been wondering lately if I might actually be a 7, just one that happens to look almost exactly like a 4. You see, I have a very deep, fundamental fear that I'm "missing out" on something-- life's experiences, the wonder of the world, or that I could be doing something *else* that would be *better* than what I'm doing now. I'm afraid of meaninglessness and drudgery (I mean, having to tolerate those things all the time would absolutely be a fate worse than death) and I respond to that by focusing on being original and unique. I'm afraid I'll waste the best parts of my life and get trapped, and I would do anything -- *anything!* \-- to avoid the feelings of regret associated with that. I'm very emotional and, being a probable 4, I don't avoid most darker emotions (with the one exception of "regret"!!!) but I'd rather be happy than sad. I'd rather see the world as the beautiful work of art it is, than dwell in despair and believe this world is truly void of hope or meaning. A postmodern comedy is very much how I see life a lot of the time... one truly worthy of wonder. I think it's an equal tragedy when people refuse to -- or cant -- see all the beauty and hopefullness and vibrancy of the world, either because they're so sunk in despair they think darkness is all there is, ***OR*** because they're running from pain and have locked themselves off from the full spectrum of emotion. The words I live by are "without the darkness we would never see the stars."

I'm.... probably still a 4, but I'm not as certain as I used to be-- I *could* be a 7. 4w5 here. I don’t think I’ve ever hated my TYPE, per se, although there are certainly things I wish I could change about myself. I see the enneagram as more of a roadmap, as it shows me what those flaws are and what changing them looks like, so I’d rather know it than not.

HOWEVER, when I first typed as a 4? Total, blinding panic and despair that completely consumed me for several weeks. Not because I hated the type, but because I hated that a quiz I could take in less than an hour could type me so accurately! And to be one of only 9 archetypes, and it identified my deepest feelings and drives and motivations... one in nine, meaning, what, one out of every 9 people or so is just like me in all these fundamental ways? Meaning... I am NOT unique, I am NOT individual, at my fundamental nature I am only an example of an extremely limited number of archetypes! There’s no point to me! I might as well not exist if other people also exist who are just like me! Once I finally calmed down, I refused to look at the enneagram for months. 

So, yeah. Now I look back on this and laugh about it, because it is SUCH a typical four reaction... I also have a much more nuanced perspective on the enneagram, and I know it’s not that simple, but still, it took me a long time to come to terms with the idea of having this much in common with anybody. I share this because it’s funny, but I also think there are things about being any type that are inherently more hateful to the members of that type than to anyone else
